fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.spec_version: ARM IHI 0031C — ARM Debug Interface v5 Architecture Specification (ADIv5). Documents ADIv5.0 (2006) + ADIv5.1 (2009 amendments) + ADIv5.2 (2017+ multi-drop SWD amendment). Maintained by Arm Limited.
previous_versions: ARM Debug Interface v4 (ADIv4) — earlier Arm debug architecture predating CoreSight; JTAG-only; no SW-DP / SWJ-DP.
ARM Debug Interface v5 (ADIv5) — released 2006 alongside CoreSight; introduced SW-DP / SWJ-DP / JTAG-DP register catalogs + MEM-AP + JTAG-AP.
ARM IHI 0031B (ADIv5.1 amendment, 2009) — added TARGETID + DLPIDR + EVENTSTAT.
ARM IHI 0031C (current, ADIv5.0/5.1/5.2 consolidated) — adds multi-drop SWD.
post_adiv5_evolution_industry_note: ARM IHI 0074 — ARM Debug Interface v6 (ADIv6) Architecture Specification (2019+). Successor to ADIv5; backward-compatible at the SW-DP / JTAG-DP wire layer but adds: 64-bit address support, extended APs (APBv4-AP, AXI4-AP, APBv5-AP), hierarchical multi-level ROM Tables, and a redesigned AP banking scheme.
ARM IHI 0029 — CoreSight Architecture Specification. Defines the ROM Table format (CoreSight ROM Table) that SWD reaches via MEM-AP.BASE.
ARM IHI 0064 — CoreSight ETM v4 Architecture Specification — defines the embedded trace macrocell whose trace exits via the SWO/TPIU pins (separate from SWD).
ARM DDI 0480F+ — Cortex-M (M0/M0+/M3/M4/M7/M33/M55) architecture reference manuals — define the Cortex-M debug-control registers (DHCSR / DCRSR / DCRDR / DEMCR) reached via SWD MEM-AP.
CMSIS-DAP — Arm's open reference firmware for a USB-to-SWD/JTAG probe (released 2013); defines the cross-vendor debug-probe protocol on top of ADIv5.

key_changes.summary: Base ADIv5 spec: 4-pin JTAG-DP + 2-pin SW-DP + mode-switchable SWJ-DP; DP registers IDCODE/ABORT/CTRL/STAT/SELECT/RDBUFF; AP layer with up to 256 APs; MEM-AP register catalog (CSW/TAR/DRW/BD0-3/BASE/IDR); JTAG-AP.
Adds TARGETID + DLPIDR + EVENTSTAT registers in DP higher banks (selected via SELECT.DPBANKSEL). Clarifies posted-read semantics. Adds DPv2 architecture version.

Multi-drop SWD: multiple SoCs share SWDIO/SWCLK; per-target selection via DP TARGETSEL transaction. Adds long-address (64-bit TAR) and large-data (≥64-bit DRW) MEM-AP variants. Adds DPv3 architecture version.

Successor architecture: full 64-bit address space; hierarchical CoreSight ROM Tables; new AP classes (APBv4-AP / APBv5-AP / AXI4-AP); reorganized banking scheme. ADIv5 SW-DP / JTAG-DP wire-layer remains compatible.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Bit 0 of DPIDR shall be hard-wired to 1 (Read-As-One) so that a stuck-at-zero SWDIO is distinguishable from a real DPIDR readout.
backward_compat_traps.trap: If a DP implementation forgets the RAO bit, the host cannot tell whether the SWD bus is even connected — a hard interop failure.
Same as DPIDR — stuck-at-zero SWDIO indistinguishable from a real TARGETID read.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Request bit 0 = Start = 1; bit 6 = Stop = 0; bit 7 = Park = 1. Any other pattern means the target shall ignore the transaction.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Custom IPs occasionally mishandle Park=1 → drive SWDIO LOW after Park → no Turnaround margin → SW-DP stuck.

backward_compat_traps.rule: ACK shall be exactly one of OK=001, WAIT=010, FAULT=100 (one-hot encoded with values 1/2/4).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Implementations that return ACK=000 or ACK=111 are protocol-non-conformant and confuse hosts; only one-hot codes 001/010/100 are valid.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Line reset shall require ≥ 50 consecutive SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Some buggy implementations only require 25 or 32 cycles; this breaks hosts that follow the spec and may falsely line-reset during a normal idle period.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Both SWJ-DP selection sequences (0xE79E and 0xE73C) shall be shifted LSB-first.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Hosts that shift MSB-first will never switch modes; this is a classic JTAG-mode bug when porting JTAG TAP code to a CMSIS-DAP probe.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The final read of an AP read burst shall be recovered via a DP.RDBUFF read.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Hosts that forget the trailing RDBUFF read get the next-to-last read result instead — off-by-one bug in nearly every first-implementation debug probe.

backward_compat_traps.rule: MEM-AP TAR auto-increment shall wrap within a 4 KB page (per spec; some MEM-AP variants relax to 1 KB or unlimited per CFG.LargeAddress).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Hosts that ignore the wrap-around boundary and continue writing across a 4 KB page boundary get DRC errors or stale TAR values.

fields.version_naming_history_note: SWD is the 2-pin variant of the ARM Debug Interface defined by ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C, first released 2006). It exists as the resource-constrained alternative to ADIv5's JTAG-DP variant. CoreSight is the umbrella debug-IP family that includes the DAP (which carries SWD/JTAG), the ROM Table format, and the various trace components (ETM/ITM/DWT/CTI/TPIU). ADIv6 (Arm IHI 0074) is the named successor, and is needed for SoCs with > 4 GB system-bus address spaces and hierarchical multi-component ROM Tables. ADIv5 remains the dominant standard across Cortex-M MCU debug as of the mid-2020s.
